A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MapReduce LoRA and RaTE research. Their complete main texts and Appendices A–F, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original image-generation, video-generation, and language-task experiments, together with merging and token-control ablations.

after.justification: v5 retains those original empirical results and adds a five-reward image-generation scaling experiment in Appendix D.3.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same expert training, iterative merging, token distillation, and inference procedures. The five-reward experiment instantiates the existing general multi-reward method without introducing a component or algorithmic adaptation.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds simultaneous alignment to five preferences on SD 3.5 M, making VQAScore and MPS optimization targets rather than only evaluation measures. This expands the alignment requirements within the existing image-generation domain; the earlier datasets and other tasks remain.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain their baseline membership, including individual experts, MORL-D/DR, Rewarded Soup, and Bone Soup. The scaling study reuses Rewarded Soup. Newly discussed FedAvg and DiLoCo are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The added five-reward experiment uses three merges and reports a requirement for 1.66 times more training steps. These are settings for an additional experiment; the previously reported training and evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 and Figure 11 add an analysis of scaling from three to five optimized rewards, showing training and merging trajectories. The existing merge-frequency, token-count, mixing-ratio, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same video evaluation with four samples per prompt and fixed shared seeds. No new repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported.

E6.justification: New Figure 11 reports final five-reward scores of 0.795 GenEval, 22.375 PickScore, 0.820 OCR, 0.895 VQAScore, and 13.672 MPS. These are additional results under expanded training objectives. Numerical entries in Tables 1–6 and the earlier plotted results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Pareto definition, averaged proximal formulation, smoothness and PL assumptions, contraction arguments, and RaTE loss remain mathematically unchanged. Differences in equation extraction and spacing do not represent revised theory.

C1.justification: The abstract and four introduction contributions retain the same claims about iterative Pareto improvement, composable token control, cross-modal performance, and untargeted-reward generalization. The shortened conclusion preserves their substance.

C2.justification: Appendix D.3 newly interprets five-reward scaling as avoiding diminishing returns and discusses optimization complexity, linear per-reward cost, and GPU-dependent wall-clock savings. Appendix F updates the demonstrated scope from three targeted preferences to five. The RaTE architecture limitation is unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 newly reports RaTE training cost as 0.1579 times MapReduce LoRA and provides relative training-cost information for five-reward scaling. Appendix C's hyperparameters, hardware, and model-access links remain unchanged; the new MORL table footnote points to existing details.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds a relationship to FedAvg and DiLoCo, distinguishing multi-preference alignment from communication-efficient training. References to A Cat Is a Cat and T2I-Copilot are also added. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v5 integrates the former Section 4.4 ablation discussion into Section 4.3, substantially shortens the conclusion, adds Appendix D.3, and makes limited wording and author-correspondence edits. Most prose and document organization are retained.

P2.justification: v5 adds the five-panel Figure 11, relocates Table 3, adds a Table 1 footnote, and adjusts equation spacing and page layout. Earlier appendix Figures 11–18 become Figures 12–19 with their visual content retained.

improvement.justification: The five-reward experiment and clearer prior-work positioning add value, but the new scalability interpretation is insufficiently supported. Appendix D.3 claims no diminishing returns relative to Figure 6, yet Figure 11's final GenEval/PickScore/OCR values are 0.795/22.375/0.820 versus 0.87/22.542/0.9158 in Figure 6 at k=4, under different training and merging settings. This does not establish a controlled performance decline, but it leaves the claimed scaling benefit unresolved. The added evidence and overinterpretation prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
